name: Federated Urban Flow
description: Urban traffic forecasting is a fundamental component of Smart Cities, yet centralized Machine Learning (ML) approaches present notable challenges regarding data privacy and communication overhead. Federated Learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving alternative to run distributed learning at the edge, but a methodological gap exists: the lack of a standardized software benchmark to systematically evaluate and compare the performance of different deep learning architectures (e.g., RNNs vs. Transformers), impeding reproducible and trustworthy research. This paper introduces Federated Urban Flow, a modular, open-source software benchmark designed specifically to probe this “model-to-application” axis. We demonstrate the benchmark's utility through a comprehensive case study involving 21 experimental scenarios. We evaluate on the public METRLA dataset using two aggregation rules (FedAvg, FedProx).
